diagnosis: Not a supersession and not a product-code regression: GET /stock correctly returns all stock records. The failure is a test-design defect in tests/step_defs/test_S2_view_home_stock_table.py::test_t21 (check_empty_array): it asserts an ABSOLUTE whole-table empty state (len(data)==0) after a 'no stock records exist' Given that does not clear the table. On the reused per-branch verify DB the 5 rows committed by S1 file-stock-record behavior tests (and S2 T17's seed) persist, so the endpoint returns them and the whole-table assertion fails. This is the shared-state-aggregate-assertion smell: t21 must OWN its state (assert a delta scoped to its own per-run SKUs, e.g. none of its run keys are present) rather than an absolute whole-table total. Fixing this needs the t21 test/scenario redesigned by the test-strategist; there is no honest product change (returning [] would break the T17 non-empty scenario).
